## Summary

This updates `docs_new/docs/references/production_metrics.mdx` into a complete browsable reference for the metrics exposed by SGLang's `/metrics` endpoint.

Changes:
- Document request, scheduler, grammar, disaggregation, HiCache/storage, LoRA, EPLB, routing-key, prefill-delayer, streaming-session, and engine metrics.
- Document common labels and feature-gated metric groups.
- Mark registered-but-currently-inactive metrics so operators do not build alerts on nominal values.
- Update the sample output from the removed `time_per_output_token_seconds` metric to `inter_token_latency_seconds`.

## Validation

- `git diff --check`
- Compared documented metric names against registered `name="sglang:..."` metrics in `python/sglang/srt/observability/metrics_collector.py`; missing/extra count is 0/0.
- `python3 scripts/ci/check_no_docs_changes.py docs_new/docs/references/production_metrics.mdx`

Docs-only change; no runtime code paths are modified.

nodes.body:
Pushed a80d7c1 addressing both review comments, plus a third correction I found while re-verifying the whole file against `main`:

1. **`queue-depth` is not a metric name** (review comment above) — replaced with the four real gauges.
2. **`per_stage_req_latency_seconds` / `queue_time_seconds` label scope** (review comment above) — both are registered on `SchedulerMetricsCollector`, so they carry the scheduler label set rather than `model_name` alone. Added a footnote with the actual labels and an aggregating PromQL example.
3. **`sglang:num_prefill_retries_total` was wrongly listed as inactive.** My original text said `increment_prefill_retries()` has no callers — that is false, it is called from `disaggregation/prefill.py:1134`. Removed it from the inactive table, dropped the dagger, and noted instead that the counter only advances when disaggregation is enabled. Thanks to the review pass for prompting the recheck; this one was my own error.

Could a maintainer add the `run-ci` label? This is docs-only (single `.mdx`, +12/-5) and I am not in `CI_PERMISSIONS.json`, so I cannot trigger CI myself — the red checks on this PR are the `Missing required label 'run-ci'` gate, not test failures.

Context for why the file needed this pass: the doc was pointing operators at `sglang:time_per_output_token_seconds`, which does not exist in the code (the metric was renamed to `sglang:inter_token_latency_seconds`). Dashboards and alerts built from the old name silently return no data, which is worst exactly when someone is debugging an incident. The PR also documents the 13 metrics that are registered but never populated, so alerts don't get built on gauges that are structurally always `0`.

Rebased onto the latest `main` and re-audited the whole reference against the current code, so the completeness claim in the description holds again rather than being true only as of when it was written.

What changed since the original audit:

**Added 40 metrics that landed in the meantime**, in their own sections where they didn't fit an existing one:

- *Encoder disaggregation* (new section) — the 10 `encoder_*` request/latency metrics plus the 7 encoder cache counters, with the `modality` / `backend` / `dp_rank` labels they actually carry.
- *HTTP server* (new section) — `http_requests_total`, `http_responses_total`, `http_requests_active`. Worth having documented separately because they count every accepted request including probes, unlike `num_requests_total`, which only counts what reaches the scheduler.
- *HiCache* — the six `hicache_backup_*` / `hicache_dropped_tokens_total` / `hicache_prefetch_aux_alloc_failed_tokens_total` / `load_back_bytes_total` metrics, with a note distinguishing the L2 (GPU → host DRAM) set from the existing L3 (`backuped_tokens_total`) one, since the names are easy to confuse.
- *Engine and process* — `startup_time_seconds`, `startup_cuda_graph_time_seconds`, `startup_latency_breakdown_seconds_max`, the three `*_memory_usage_gb` gauges, and `process_cpu_seconds_total`.
- Plus `prefill_effective_tokens_total`, `max_total_num_tokens_swa`, `routing_keys_active`, `spec_block_accept_length`, `spec_cap_length`, `failed_session_recoveries_total`.

**Removed 2 metrics that no longer exist**: `engine_startup_time` and `engine_load_weights_time`, dropped in #33375. There's a short note pointing readers to `startup_time_seconds` (phase-labelled, so weight loading is now a phase rather than its own metric) so anyone with an existing dashboard can find the replacement.

Also flagged the metrics whose labels differ from the section default — `startup_latency_breakdown_seconds_max`, `process_cpu_seconds_total`, and `routing_keys_active` don't carry the scheduler label set, which silently breaks queries that assume they do.

Verification: the registered set and the documented set now match exactly at 152/152 (0 missing, 0 stale), checked by extracting every `"sglang:..."` registration from `python/sglang/` and diffing against the page, accounting for histogram-derived `_bucket`/`_sum`/`_count` series.

Docs-only, no runtime changes. @merrymercy @hnyls2002 — should be a quick one.

**On the red checks:** they're `pr-gate` / `pr-test-*-finish` failing because the PR has no `run-ci` label, not any real failure — I'm not in `.github/CI_PERMISSIONS.json`, so I can't add it myself. Could a maintainer add it?

Following the merge process in [MAINTAINER.md](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md): this PR never got past step 2. No Merge Oncall was ever assigned (the assignee list is empty), and without step 3 the `run-ci` label was never applied — so the red checks are `pr-gate` refusing to start, and no test has ever actually run on this branch.

Step 4 says the author may ping other related Merge Oncalls when the assigned one is unresponsive, so per the CI, Release, Package area: @Kangyan-Zhou @Fridge003 — could one of you assign an oncall and add `run-ci` (or `/tag-and-rerun-ci`)? I'm not in `.github/CI_PERMISSIONS.json`, so I can't trigger it myself.

Thanks @anencore94. Closing this because you have 9 PRs open and none updated in 7 days, over our soft cap of 5 for idle PRs.

Reopen the two or three you most want reviewed - a short active set moves faster than a long idle one.

Some directories moved recently, so an older branch may need retargeting:
`sgl-kernel/` -> `python/sglang/kernels/aot/`, `python/sglang/jit_kernel/`
-> `python/sglang/kernels/jit/`, `docs/` -> `docs/docs/` (`.mdx`),
`bench_serving.py` -> `benchmark/serving.py`, `test/srt/` -> `test/registered/`.

## Code Review

This pull request updates the documentation in `docs/references/production_metrics.md` by renaming the `time_per_output_token_seconds` metric to `inter_token_latency_seconds` and adding a comprehensive "Metrics Reference" section detailing all exposed Prometheus metrics, their types, labels, and enablement conditions. The review feedback suggests correcting the non-existent `queue-depth` metric name to `num_*_queue_reqs` and clarifying that `sglang:per_stage_req_latency_seconds` and `sglang:queue_time_seconds` carry scheduler/engine labels rather than request labels.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> The [consumer version of Gemini Code Assist on GitHub](https://developers.google.com/gemini-code-assist/docs/review-repo-code) is being sunset. Starting **June 18, 2026**, new organization installations will be blocked, and all code review activity will officially cease on **July 17, 2026**.
> For more details on the timeline and next steps, please review the [Help Documentation](https://developers.google.com/gemini-code-assist/docs/deprecations/consumer-code-review).

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

The metric name `queue-depth` does not exist. The actual metrics tracking queue depths in disaggregation mode are named `sglang:num_prefill_bootstrap_queue_reqs`, `sglang:num_prefill_inflight_queue_reqs`, `sglang:num_decode_prealloc_queue_reqs`, and `sglang:num_decode_transfer_queue_reqs`. We should use the pattern `num_*_queue_reqs` to be consistent with actual metric names.

```suggestion
| Prefill/Decode disaggregation | disaggregation mode enabled | num_*_queue_reqs, kv_transfer_*, num_bootstrap_failed_reqs_total, num_transfer_failed_reqs_total |
```

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

The metrics `sglang:per_stage_req_latency_seconds` and `sglang:queue_time_seconds` are registered in `SchedulerMetricsCollector` rather than `TokenizerMetricsCollector`. Consequently, they carry the scheduler/engine common labels (such as `engine_type`, `tp_rank`, `pp_rank`, `moe_ep_rank`) instead of the request metrics common labels (which only carry `model_name`). We should clarify this in their descriptions so operators know what labels to expect.

```suggestion
| `sglang:per_stage_req_latency_seconds` | Histogram | `stage` | Latency of each stage of a request's lifecycle. Note: This is a scheduler metric and carries scheduler/engine labels. |
| `sglang:queue_time_seconds` | Histogram | | Histogram of queueing time in seconds. Note: This is a scheduler metric and carries scheduler/engine labels. |
```

Fixed in a80d7c1. Replaced `queue-depth` with the four actual gauges: `num_prefill_bootstrap_queue_reqs`, `num_prefill_inflight_queue_reqs`, `num_decode_prealloc_queue_reqs`, `num_decode_transfer_queue_reqs`.

Fixed in a80d7c1. Kept both rows in the request-lifecycle table but marked them with a footnote spelling out the scheduler label set (`model_name`, `engine_type`, `tp_rank`, `pp_rank`, `moe_ep_rank`, plus `dp_rank` under data parallelism), with an aggregating PromQL example so queries written from this doc don't hit a label mismatch.

+The snippet above is only a small illustrative sample. The complete list of
+metrics exposed by the server is documented in the
+[Metrics Reference](#metrics-reference) below.
+
+## Metrics Reference
+
+This section lists every metric exposed on the `/metrics` endpoint, grouped by
+area. The **Type** column uses Prometheus metric types (`Counter`, `Gauge`,
+`Histogram`, `Summary`). Any labels listed in **Extra labels** are attached in
+addition to the common labels described below.
+
+> **Metric activity.** Most metrics below are actively populated during normal
+> operation. A handful are currently **inactive** — they are registered on the
+> endpoint but the code path that would populate them is not wired up, so they
+> always report their default value (or are never emitted). Inactive metrics are
+> marked with a dagger (`†`) in the tables and listed together under
+> [Currently inactive metrics](#currently-inactive-metrics). Feature-gated
+> metrics (see [Enablement flags](#enablement-flags)) are *not* inactive — they
+> are populated with real values once their feature is turned on.
+
+### Labels
+
+Two collectors emit metrics, each with its own set of common labels applied to
+every metric it exports:
+
+- **Request metrics** (emitted from the tokenizer/API-server process) carry
+  `model_name`.
+- **Scheduler / engine metrics** carry `model_name`, `engine_type`, `tp_rank`,
+  `pp_rank`, and `moe_ep_rank`. `dp_rank` is added when data parallelism is
+  enabled.
+
+Additional common labels can appear depending on server configuration:
+
+- `priority` — added to all metrics when `--enable-priority-scheduling` is set.
+- Custom labels from `--extra-metric-labels` (both collectors) and
+  `--tokenizer-metrics-allowed-custom-labels` (request metrics).
+
+### Enablement flags
+
+Some metrics are only created when the corresponding feature is turned on:
+
+| Feature | Flag / condition | Metrics |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| MFU estimation | `--enable-mfu-metrics` | `estimated_flops_per_gpu_total`, `estimated_read_bytes_per_gpu_total`, `estimated_write_bytes_per_gpu_total` |
+| LoRA | LoRA serving enabled | `lora_pool_slots_used`, `lora_pool_slots_total`, `lora_pool_utilization` |
+| Hierarchical (Hi)Cache | `--enable-hierarchical-cache` | `hicache_host_used_tokens`, `hicache_host_total_tokens`, `evicted_tokens_total`, `eviction_duration_seconds`, `load_back_tokens_total`, `load_back_duration_seconds` |
+| L3 / storage tier | storage backend enabled | `prefetched_tokens_total`, `backuped_tokens_total`, `prefetch_pgs`, `backup_pgs`, `prefetch_bandwidth`, `backup_bandwidth` |
+| Prefill/Decode disaggregation | disaggregation mode enabled | `num_prefill_bootstrap_queue_reqs`, `num_prefill_inflight_queue_reqs`, `num_decode_prealloc_queue_reqs`, `num_decode_transfer_queue_reqs`, `kv_transfer_*`, `num_bootstrap_failed_reqs_total`, `num_transfer_failed_reqs_total`, `num_prefill_retries_total` |
+| Per-device forward timing | `SGLANG_ENABLE_METRICS_DEVICE_TIMER=1` | `forward_execution_seconds_total`, `dp_cooperation_forward_execution_seconds_total` |
+| Expert parallelism load balancing | `SGLANG_ENABLE_EPLB_BALANCEDNESS_METRIC=1` (MoE, `moe_ep_rank == 0`) | `eplb_balancedness` |
+| EPLB heatmap | `SGLANG_EPLB_HEATMAP_COLLECTION_INTERVAL > 0` | `eplb_gpu_physical_count` |
+| Streaming sessions | `--enable-streaming-session` | `num_streaming_sessions`, `streaming_session_held_tokens` |
+| Encoder disaggregation | encoder runtime enabled (separate multimodal encode stage) | `encoder_*`, including the encoder cache counters |
+
+### Currently inactive metrics
+
+The following metrics are registered on the `/metrics` endpoint but are **not
+currently populated** by any code path — they always report their default value
+(e.g. `0`) or are never emitted at all. They are kept here for completeness and
+so operators do not build alerts on top of them expecting live data. Each is
+also marked with `†` in the tables below.
+
+| Metric | Reason it is inactive |
+| --- | --- |
+| `sglang:utilization` | Only computed when `max_running_requests_under_SLO` is set, which never happens; stays `0` (or `-1` in prefill-disaggregation mode). |
+| `sglang:max_running_requests_under_SLO` | Source value is never assigned anywhere, so the gauge is never emitted. |
+| `sglang:pending_prealloc_token_usage` | Backing `SchedulerStats` field is never populated; always `0`. |
+| `sglang:is_cuda_graph` | Backing `SchedulerStats` field is never populated; superseded by `cuda_graph_passes_total`. |
+| `sglang:num_grammar_total` | Populated only by `log_grammar_stats()`, which has no callers. |
+| `sglang:num_grammar_cache_hit_total` | Populated only by `log_grammar_stats()`, which has no callers. |
+| `sglang:num_grammar_aborted_total` | Populated only by `log_grammar_stats()`, which has no callers. |
+| `sglang:num_grammar_timeout_total` | Populated only by `log_grammar_stats()`, which has no callers. |
+| `sglang:grammar_compilation_time_seconds` | Populated only by `log_grammar_stats()`, which has no callers. |
+| `sglang:grammar_schema_count` | Populated only by `log_grammar_stats()`, which has no callers. |
+| `sglang:grammar_ebnf_size` | Populated only by `log_grammar_stats()`, which has no callers. |
+| `sglang:grammar_tree_traversal_time_avg` | Populated only by `log_grammar_stats()`, which has no callers. |
+| `sglang:grammar_tree_traversal_time_max` | Populated only by `log_grammar_stats()`, which has no callers. |

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

The metric name `queue-depth` does not exist. The actual metrics tracking queue depths in disaggregation mode are named `sglang:num_prefill_bootstrap_queue_reqs`, `sglang:num_prefill_inflight_queue_reqs`, `sglang:num_decode_prealloc_queue_reqs`, and `sglang:num_decode_transfer_queue_reqs`. We should use the pattern `num_*_queue_reqs` to be consistent with actual metric names.

```suggestion
| Prefill/Decode disaggregation | disaggregation mode enabled | num_*_queue_reqs, kv_transfer_*, num_bootstrap_failed_reqs_total, num_transfer_failed_reqs_total |
```

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

The metrics `sglang:per_stage_req_latency_seconds` and `sglang:queue_time_seconds` are registered in `SchedulerMetricsCollector` rather than `TokenizerMetricsCollector`. Consequently, they carry the scheduler/engine common labels (such as `engine_type`, `tp_rank`, `pp_rank`, `moe_ep_rank`) instead of the request metrics common labels (which only carry `model_name`). We should clarify this in their descriptions so operators know what labels to expect.

```suggestion
| `sglang:per_stage_req_latency_seconds` | Histogram | `stage` | Latency of each stage of a request's lifecycle. Note: This is a scheduler metric and carries scheduler/engine labels. |
| `sglang:queue_time_seconds` | Histogram | | Histogram of queueing time in seconds. Note: This is a scheduler metric and carries scheduler/engine labels. |
```

Fixed in a80d7c1. Replaced `queue-depth` with the four actual gauges: `num_prefill_bootstrap_queue_reqs`, `num_prefill_inflight_queue_reqs`, `num_decode_prealloc_queue_reqs`, `num_decode_transfer_queue_reqs`.

Fixed in a80d7c1. Kept both rows in the request-lifecycle table but marked them with a footnote spelling out the scheduler label set (`model_name`, `engine_type`, `tp_rank`, `pp_rank`, `moe_ep_rank`, plus `dp_rank` under data parallelism), with an aggregating PromQL example so queries written from this doc don't hit a label mismatch.

2. **`per_stage_req_latency_seconds` / `queue_time_seconds` label scope** (review comment above) — both are registered on `SchedulerMetricsCollector`, so they carry the scheduler label set rather than `model_name` alone. Added a footnote with the actual labels and an aggregating PromQL example.
3. **`sglang:num_prefill_retries_total` was wrongly listed as inactive.** My original text said `increment_prefill_retries()` has no callers — that is false, it is called from `disaggregation/prefill.py:1134`. Removed it from the inactive table, dropped the dagger, and noted instead that the counter only advances when disaggregation is enabled.
